 accommodations must be received 72 hours prior to the day of the Council Meetings.

Inglewood, California
  October 29, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, October 29, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
  the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
  Authority, Finance Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at
  the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The Acting City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority
  Secretary/Finance Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman/Finance  Authority
  Chairman/Parking  Authority  Chairman/Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority  Members/Finance  Authority
  Members/Parking  Authority  Members/Joint
  Powers Authority Members Padilla, Morales, and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  Council  Member/Successor  Agency
  Member/Housing Authority Member/Finance
  Authority  Member/Parking  Authority
  Member/Joint Powers Authority Member Dotson.
  City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority / Finance Authority / Parking
  Authority /Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Cheryl Moore  Management Assistant

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

180  COMMENDATION – HONORING STILL I RISE FROM CANCER, INC.
  The City Council presented Still I Rise from Cancer, with a commendation
  recognizing their outstanding efforts to the community. The representative from
  Still I Rise from Cancer, Inc., thanked the City Council for recognizing their
  organization.

180  PRESENTATION – HONORING THE FIVE INGLEWOOD LIBRARY’S
  CAREER ONLINE HIGH SCHOOL GRADUATES. Linda Silba recognized
  the following persons for completing their online high school diplomas:

    Jimmy Ruiz (present at ceremony)
    Ida Martiani (present at ceremony)
    Janice Bennett (present at ceremony)
    Ramon Llamas
    Robert Gonzalez

  1
 October 29, 2019

 180  PRESENTATION – SENATOR STEVEN C. BRADFORD. Senator Bradford
  provided a legislative update on important bills affecting the constituents of the
  35th District.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking
  Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there
  were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor

  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  The following persons spoke concerning CI-1, Initiative by Mayor James T.
  Butts, Jr., recommending the introduction of an Ordinance to amend Chapter 8 of
  the Inglewood Municipal Code by adding Article 9 (Just Cause Eviction
  Protections), Article 10 (Residential Rent Regulations); and Chapter 2, Article 3
  (Boards and Commissions) to add a Rental Housing Board.

  Phoebe Crenshaw
  Yvonne (No Last Name Given)
  Johnathon Yeager
  Katherine Bennett

  Jorge Rivera

  Willie Agee

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Padilla that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated October 25, 2019, in the amount of
  $1,433,598.31, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority
  Member Dotson.

 301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 20-02 INTRODUCED –
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2019-001 (ZCA 2019-001) TO CHAPTER
  12 (PLANNING AND ZONING) TO ALLOW TOWING SERVICE WITH
  ANCILLARY VEHICLE STORAGE AND ANCILLARY VEHICLE
  INSPECTION. The Acting City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter is a
  public hearing to consider an ordinance approving Zoning Code Amendment
  2019-001 (ZCA-2019-001) to Chapter 12 (Planning and Zoning) of the Inglewood
  Municipal Code to allow towing service with ancillary vehicle storage and
  ancillary vehicle inspection in the C-S (Commercial Storage) zone citywide, that
  notice has been given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, and that
  no communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated October 29, 2019.

  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager, gave a brief report.

  2
 October 29, 2019

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the
  City Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member Padilla that the City Council does hereby Affirm Categorical
  Exemption (EA-CE-2019-091). The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Furthermore, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Franklin, that further reading be waived. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 20-02 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, TO APPROVE ZONIG CODE
  AMENDMENT 2019-001 (ZCA-2019-001) TO AMEND ARTICLE 9
  OF CHAPTER 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO MODIFY PERMITTED USES
  FOR THE C-S (COMMERCIAL SERVICE) ZONE CITYWIDE

  was introduced by Council Member Franklin.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending

  a) Azusena Favela for alleged personal injury and unlawful detention on March
  16, 2019.
  b) California Auto Insurance subro Sandra Sunabria for alleged vehicle damage
  on August 18, 2019.
  c) Tina Pool for alleged property damage on June 22, 2019. *

  *Amended Claim

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member
  Padilla, and carried that the above listed claims be rejected.

  125  RESOLUTION NO. 20-04 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2019-2020
  FISCAL YEAR BUDGET TO SECURE LEGAL SERVICES OF BREMER
  WHYTE BROWN & O’MEARA. Staff report dated October 29, 2019, was

  2020 annual budget transferring $50,000 from General Fund Reserves to secure
  the legal services of Bremer Whyte Brown & O’Meara.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that Resolution No. 20-04 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2019-2020 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  RECEIVE FUNDS TO ENGAGE SPECIAL COUNSEL FOR VARIOUS
  LEGAL SERVICES

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

 October 29, 2019

  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent:  Council Member Dotson.

 125  AGREEMENT NO. 20-20 APPROVED – KANE BALLMER &
  BERKMAN; RESOLUTION NO. 20-05 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE

  presented recommending approval of an agreement with Kane Ballmer &

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member

  A RESOLUITON OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on October
  1, 2019, October 8, 2019, and October 15, 2019, be approved. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  301  AGREEMENT NO. 20-021 APPROVED – DUDEK; RESOLUTION NO. 20-

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT EVALUATION

  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  178  AGREEMENT NO. 20-023 APPROVED – BEAR COMMUNICATIONS.
  Staff report dated October 29, 2019, was presented recommending approval of a
  two-year agreement (with the option to extend two additional one-year terms)

 October 29, 2019

  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes:  None; and

  5
 October 29, 2019

 219  ORAL REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. Wanda Brown, City Treasurer,
  invited students to take part in her Student Treasurer’s Academy Program
  beginning November 6, 2019 through November 23, 2019. She also reminded
  women to make sure they have their breast exams.

 127.1  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Mayor Butts:

  Initiative by Mayor James T. Butts, Jr., recommending the introduction of an
  Ordinance to amend Chapter 8 of the Inglewood Municipal Code by adding
  Article 9 (Just Cause Eviction Protections), Article 10 (Residential Rent
  Regulations); and Chapter 2, Article 3 (Boards and Commissions) to add a Rental
  Housing Board.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the
  City Council does hereby sunset the date for rental increases of 3% or CPI
  (whichever is greater), and 5% or CPI for dwellings deemed at least 80% under
  Fair Market Value to December 31, 2024; after which, the rental increases for all
  properties, beginning January 1, 2025, will mirror that of the allowable state
  increase (still under City Control). The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the
  City Council does hereby strike and delete the verbiage on page 19, lines 22 and
  23 which reads “The Board members shall select amongst themselves a
  Chairperson and Vice Chairperson.” The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby waive further reading. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 20-03 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING CHAPTER 8 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO ADD ARTICLE 10 (RESIDENTIAL RENT
  REGULATIONS); AMENDING CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 3
  (BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS) TO ADD A RENTAL HOUSING
  BOARD; AND AMENDING CHAPTER 9, ARTICLE 1 (GENERAL
  PROVISIONS) TO CHANGE THE DEFINITION OF “TRANSIENT.”

  was introduced by Council Member Morales.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Wild Bill Widner gave suggestions regarding the MTA Greenline.

  6
 October 29, 2019

  Rayhab Mitchell stated she would like to see the lights on Manchester and
  Century, and Manchester and Grevillea held longer for pedestrians to cross

  LaTosha Bailey stated she is concerned about the trees at Edward Vincent Park
  that are on the electrical wires.

  Willie Agee commented he is disappointed with Madison Square Garden.

  Stuart Bailey commented he is looking forward to the Clippers coming to
  Inglewood.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts adjourned the
